verdict.rationale: LangGraph documents interrupts that pause graph execution at specific points and wait for external input. Execution resumes by re-invoking the graph with Command, whose value becomes the return of interrupt(). Breakpoints are set at compile time, and checkpointers persist state for human-in-the-loop workflows. Together these let a team gate sensitive tool-executing nodes behind human approval, and community commentary confirms human-in-the-loop is a core strength. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of per-tool approval gating (approve/edit/reject of a specific tool call), a policy-level way to designate which tools require approval, and hands-on corroboration of tool-call approval specifically.
